questions.q: What is Lakeflow, at a high level?
options: Databricks' current, unified umbrella term for ingestion, declarative pipeline definitions, and orchestration as one coherent system
A completely new Spark engine replacing everything covered so far
A third-party tool unrelated to Databricks
questions.explain: This addresses the exact gap Lesson 47 flagged — separately-managed pieces, now unified.

questions.q: What older Databricks name refers to the same feature as "Lakeflow Declarative Pipelines"?
questions.explain: Real, current documentation and existing production code still often reference DLT by that older name.

questions.q: Which of this course's earlier concepts maps to Lakeflow Connect?
questions.explain: Lakeflow Connect is Lakeflow's name for the managed ingestion piece this course already built.

questions.q: Which earlier course concept maps to Lakeflow Jobs?
options: Jobs and chained tasks from Lessons 11 and 29-30
questions.explain: Lakeflow Jobs is the orchestration piece — the same task-chaining concept, given a unified product name.

questions.q: Is Lakeflow introducing entirely new concepts the course hasn't already covered?
options: Yes, Lakeflow requires abandoning Unity Catalog
Yes, Lakeflow replaces Delta Lake entirely
Yes, everything in this chapter is unrelated to prior chapters
No — it's this course's own Chapters 1-4 material, given a real product name and a more declarative way to express it
questions.explain: Autoloader, foreachBatch/MERGE pipeline logic, and jobs/tasks all map directly onto Lakeflow's three pieces.
